commits.message:
claude-sessions counts a line skipped only when a record failed to parse (rich-demos-k78j.zs7)

loadSession counted every blank line as skipped, so the newline that ends
every JSONL file showed as '(1 lines skipped)' on every session opened in
Node. A blank line carries no record; only a non-blank line that fails to
parse is now counted.

A host can ask when what it draws next changes (rich-animation-xi28.6rs) (#416)

* A host can ask when what it draws next changes (rich-animation-xi28.6rs)

* systemClock.at ticks only once the clock reads the time

Review (medium, post-rebase) on PR #416.

A platform timer is due by the event loop's millisecond-truncated time,
so it ran while performance.now() still read under the time asked for,
by up to most of a millisecond. A Live waking at a frame's end then drew
the old frame again and waited again, at every boundary. The wait is now
rounded up and a timer that ran early is armed again for the remainder,
in the clock, once, for every host.

Style.toString's docstring claimed a round-trip through parse; meta,
anchor and nextChange have no spelling, so it now says it is the look.

* The stepped-ink cost test samples the step's first frame as it samples the rest

CI failed its one-sample assertion by 0.7%: a lone first-frame timing against a median of 59. Nine fresh signals' first frames are taken and their median compared, so one sample's jitter decides nothing. The contract asserted is unchanged.

* The shape-card spec finds the Effect shape block by its interface line

docs/effects.md's shape block is `interface Effect {` now that an effect may say when its frame next changes; the spec looked for `type Effect =` and found no card.
Emphasis closes outside every tighter construct, and link destinations read escapes (rich-unfiled-791c.5r6q)

Markdown drops inline HTML where Rich does, and reads backslash escapes (rich-unfiled-791c.5r6q)

markdown-it-py's HTML_TAG_RE — a tag, comment, processing instruction,
declaration or CDATA section — is read inline and drawn as nothing. The
block kind for a lone tag and the inline rule now share one tag grammar.

The escape rule comes with it: markdown-it reads '\<' at the backslash
before html_inline sees the '<', so without it '\<span>' would draw '\'
where Rich draws '<span>'.

Unclosed openers scan to the end of the text from every '<', as
markdown-it-py's own regex does.
